summary: Yellowstone lookout on Bunsen Peak, first reported in a 1940 newspaper item; now listed as a gone shelter, with no removal date or site description in the sources.

facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association list and firelookout.com both mark it gone. Neither gives a date or describes how it ended.

access.note: The summit is reached by a trail in Yellowstone National Park, per the NPS overlook page. That page does not mention the lookout; the access level is inferred from the trail.

visit.trail_note: NPS describes a moderate 4.2-mile (6.7-km) there-and-back trail to the summit, with a warning about grizzly bears.

events.note: Newspaper says additional fire lookouts were 'established' in August 1940, one of them at Bunsen Peak. The source gives no build date.

evidence.supports: page heading places the site in Yellowstone National Park
1940 newspaper item: additional lookouts established, one at Bunsen Peak
evidence.quote: Additional fire lookouts were established--including one at Bunsen peak

evidence.supports: lookouts added for the first time in several years because of hazardous conditions
evidence.quote: for the first time in several years, because of the hazardous conditions in the park timber and range.

evidence.supports: about two miles south of Mammoth Hot Springs
evidence.quote: 2 miles south of Mammoth Hot Springs

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association list: type Shelter, status Gone
NPS: moderate 4.2-mile there-and-back trail to the summit
evidence.quote: A moderate 4.2-mile (6.7-km) there-and-back trail to the summit of Bunsen Peak.
CAUTION: Grizzly bears frequent this area.

corrections.why: The FFLA Wyoming list gives the type of the Bunsen Peak site as Shelter, not ground. Firelookout.com gives no type, so the list is the only source for it.

sources.title: Bunsen Peak - FOREST LOOKOUTS (quoting The Salt Lake Tribune, August 20, 1940)

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one 1940 newspaper item, read through westlookouts, which reprints it (the Tribune original was not read), and two lists that say gone with no date. The source spells the place 'Mammath'; the story uses the correct spelling and quotes nothing with the typo. A social post by Yellowstone Wildlife Profiles on Facebook says the 1988 North Fork Fire moved across Bunsen Peak toward Mammoth; it is not used, since it is a social post. The NPS 1988 fires page (https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/nature/1988-fires.htm) turned up in search but was not read, and may say whether the lookout was involved. The access level rests on the NPS trail page, not on any statement about the lookout site. No photo added: firelookout.com credits the National Park Service Archives but gives no image URL.
